entity.name: David W
entity.description: Software engineer based in Nairobi, Kenya. Maintainer of OpenUSSD and of three plugins on the WordPress.org plugin directory (Doctor Subs, Draft Order Control, EdgeMail). Works in open source day to day.

projects.name: OpenUSSD
projects.description: An open-source, self-hosted gateway and SDK for developers and public-interest organisations that run USSD services and want to own them, across providers and with their data on their own servers. SMS and direct network connections over SMPP are planned. Three components: a self-hostable gateway with multi-tenant routing and one telco-adapter interface over networks and aggregators; SDKs for building USSD applications as state machines with typed sessions, i18n, and screens measured in the encoding the network uses (182 GSM-7 characters, or 70 UCS-2); and a reference adapter that exposes ActivityPub Fediverse content through USSD menus. v0.1 ships the gateway, the Go SDK and a read-only Mastodon adapter; a TypeScript SDK is planned. Aimed at Sub-Saharan Africa, where 60% of mobile internet subscribers still use feature phones or 3G smartphones (GSMA 2025).

channels.description: Direct outreach for grant programmes, sponsorship, or pilot partnerships. The maintainer will reply with the most appropriate channel (bank transfer, OpenCollective, GitHub Sponsors, or grant invoicing) for each conversation.

plans.name: Core development to v1.0
plans.description: About seven months of development, 1,250 hours at EUR 40 an hour, in six work packages: a production-ready gateway; SMPP, MTN and a second aggregator adapter; SMS; a TypeScript SDK and developer guides; Fediverse posting and account linking; and a v1.0 release with the findings of an independent security audit fixed and two pilots in Kenya. Every euro pays for development time. The task-by-task plan is in ROADMAP.md.

plans.name: Ongoing maintenance and ecosystem support
plans.description: Recurring support after v1.0: security patching, new MNO adapters, Fediverse-protocol updates, community engagement, and pilot integrations. Any monthly amount helps keep the gateway and SDKs maintained.
